reference.purpose: Adds a vibrant green color and a tart, tropical sweetness. It is the iconic topping for an Australian Pavlova.
reference.storage: Store at room temperature until soft, then move to the fridge.
reference.usageTips: Did You Know? You can't use fresh kiwifruit in jelly. The enzymes will eat the gelatine and stop the jelly from ever setting. Always use kiwifruit as a topper, never mixed into the set.

reference.notes: Kumquats are small citrus fruits that can be eaten whole, skin and all. - ** Can be zested for extra citrus flavor. Ideal for marmalades, desserts, candied preparations, glazes, and salads. Can also be pickled or added to cocktails and drinks. - **Pairings:** Complements honey, ginger, gin, brandy, other citrus, and fresh herbs. - ** Wash before consumption. - **Substitutions:** Other small citrus like calamansi or kumquat hybrids can be used, though flavor varies.
reference.purpose: Adds tart-sweet flavor, bright color, and aromatic zest to desserts, marmalades, glazes, salads, and beverages.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place or refrigerate to extend freshness.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Eat fresh, sliced, or whole; remove seeds if desired.

reference.notes: Use cuts suitable for slow cooking to achieve tenderness and enhance flavor. Popular cuts include shoulder, shank, neck, and leg. - ** Can be marinated to enhance flavor. - **Pairings:** Complements garlic, rosemary, thyme, cumin, coriander, yogurt, and root vegetables. - ** Keep in airtight packaging to prevent freezer burn. - **Substitutions:** Beef or goat can be used in place of lamb, though flavor and tenderness differ.
reference.purpose: Adds rich, gamey flavor, moisture, and protein to curries, stews, and slow-cooked dishes.

reference.notes: The most expensive and prized cut of the lamb. They are essentially individual steaks from the rib rack.
reference.purpose: A premium, tender 'lollipop' of meat that is perfect for quick grilling or pan-searing.
reference.storage: Use within 2 days of purchase.
reference.usageTips: The fat on the edge is the best part! Stand the cutlets on their 'backs' in the pan for 1 minute to render the fat until it's crispy and golden.

reference.notes: Also known as BBQ chops. Because they come from the shoulder area, the meat has more connective tissue which results in a deeper 'lamb' flavor.
reference.purpose: An affordable and incredibly flavorful cut. They are fattier than loin chops, making them ideal for slow-grilling or braising.
reference.storage: Refrigerate for 2-3 days.
reference.usageTips: These chops are best cooked 'Medium' to 'Well-Done' to allow the fat to render properly. If you cook them rare, the fat will be chewy and unpleasant.

reference.notes: Can be bought 'Bone-in' (for better flavor) or 'Boneless/Butterflied' (for faster cooking and easier carving).
reference.purpose: The classic Sunday Roast cut. It provides a huge amount of lean, flavorful meat for feeding a crowd.
reference.storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days.
reference.usageTips: Don't carve it immediately! A whole leg of lamb needs at least 15-20 minutes of resting time under foil. If you cut it too soon, all the delicious juices will run out onto the board.

reference.notes: A rack consists of 8 ribs. When the fat and meat are cleaned off the bone tips, it is called a 'Frenched' rack.
reference.purpose: The 'centerpiece' cut. It provides the most tender, succulent meat with a sophisticated presentation.
reference.storage: Use within 2 days.
reference.usageTips: Always sear the fat-cap in a hot pan first to render it down before moving the rack to the oven. This ensures the fat is crispy rather than rubbery when the meat is cooked medium-rare.

reference.notes: Usually sliced from the leg or back-strap. Because they are thin, they cook in under 3 minutes.
reference.purpose: Designed for fast cooking. They provide a juicy, gamey protein for stir-fries, souvlakis, or salads.
reference.storage: Use within 24 hours.
reference.usageTips: To get a good sear without boiling the meat, make sure the lamb is at room temperature and the pan is smoking hot. Cook in small batches so the pan temperature doesn't drop.

reference.notes: Flat, rectangular sheets of egg or durum wheat pasta used to build the classic layered Italian dish. Available dried (requiring pre-cooking or oven-ready) or fresh. Dried sheets are firm and hold their structure well during baking; oven-ready or instant varieties absorb liquid from the sauce and soften during cooking without pre-boiling. Fresh sheets are delicate and cook faster but produce a softer, more tender result. Store dried pasta in a cool, dry place indefinitely; fresh pasta should be refrigerated and used within days.
reference.purpose: Provides the structural layers in lasagne, creating distinct strata of pasta, sauce, and cheese. Absorbs and holds sauce while maintaining a tender but firm bite when properly cooked.

reference.notes: Unlike large 'Continental' cucumbers, Lebanese cucumbers don't need to be peeled and are small enough to be eaten whole.
reference.purpose: The standard Australian lunchbox cucumber. It provides a sweet, thin skin and a crunchy, near-seedless interior.
reference.storage: Keep in the fridge, but keep them dry! If they sit in moisture, they turn mushy and develop soft spots within days.
reference.usageTips: Because the skin is so thin, they absorb dressings very quickly. Slice them right before serving to ensure they stay crunchy rather than becoming pickled in the salad bowl.

reference.notes: A mild, sweet member of the onion family with a long white stalk that transitions to flat, dark green leaves. More delicate and less pungent than brown onions. The white and light green parts are tender and ideal for cooking; the dark green tops are tougher but excellent for stocks and broths. Must be thoroughly washed before use as soil gets trapped between the tightly packed layers — slice first, then rinse in a colander. Commonly sautéed as an aromatic base, braised as a side, or used in soups and stews. Store unwashed in the refrigerator for up to a week.
reference.purpose: Adds a gentle, sweet onion flavour without the sharpness of regular onions. Functions as an aromatic base in soups and stews, or as a vegetable component in Filipino dishes like bulalo.

reference.notes: Leg ham is cured and usually cooked. 'Off the bone' ham is generally superior in texture and flavor to processed 'sandwich' hams.
reference.purpose: Provides a salty, smoky, and high-quality protein. It is the king of the Australian Christmas table.
reference.storage: Store in a 'Ham Bag' (a damp calico bag) in the fridge. This allows the ham to breathe without drying out.
reference.usageTips: If you are roasting a whole leg ham, score the fat into diamonds and stud each point with a whole clove. Brush with a mix of honey and mustard for a classic glaze.

reference.notes: Lemon zest is the outer colored peel of a lemon, rich in aromatic oils. - ** Ideal for flavoring cakes, cookies, custards, glazes, sauces, dressings, and beverages. - **Pairings:** Complements sugar, honey, chocolate, berries, cream, herbs like thyme or basil, and other citrus. - ** - **Substitutions:** Lemon extract or finely grated lime zest can be used, though flavor will differ slightly.
reference.purpose: Adds bright, fresh citrus aroma and flavor, enhancing desserts, baked goods, sauces, and beverages.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store fresh zest in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to a few days, or freeze for longer storage.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use only the colored peel; avoid the bitter white pith.

reference.notes: Refer to Juice entry in main inventory.
reference.purpose: Adds bright acidity to balance sweetness in desserts, glazes, drinks, and dressings.

reference.notes: The standard soy sauce used in most Asian cooking. Thinner and saltier than dark soy sauce with a lighter brown colour and a clean, salty-savoury flavour. Made from fermented soybeans and wheat. Used for seasoning, marinating, dipping, and as the primary salty element in stir-fries, sauces, and dressings. Adds salt and umami without darkening the dish significantly.
reference.purpose: Adds saltiness, umami, and savoury depth without significantly changing the colour of a dish. The primary seasoning soy sauce for everyday cooking, marinades, and dipping sauces.
reference.storage: Store in a cool, dry place; refrigerate after opening for longest freshness.

reference.notes: Lime juice is the key to 'cooking' fish without heat in dishes like Ceviche. The acid changes the structure of the fish protein.
reference.purpose: Adds a sharp, zesty acidity. It is more 'aromatic' and tropical than lemon juice, making it essential for Thai and Mexican food.
reference.storage: Store whole limes in the fridge to keep them from drying out.
reference.usageTips: Roll your lime on the counter with the palm of your hand before cutting it. This breaks the tiny juice sacs inside and helps you get up to 20% more juice out of the fruit.

reference.notes: Linseed, also known as flaxseed, can be used whole or ground. - ** Ground linseed can help bind ingredients and improve moisture retention in gluten-free baking. - **Pairings:** Works well with oats, nuts, seeds, honey, fruits, and other flours. - ** Ground linseed is best refrigerated to prevent rancidity. - **Substitutions:** Chia seeds, hemp seeds, or sesame seeds can be used for similar texture and nutritional benefits.
reference.purpose: Adds fiber, omega-3 fatty acids, protein, and nutty flavor. Enhances texture and nutritional profile in breads and baked goods.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dark place in an airtight container.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Add to breads, muffins, granola, or smoothies for texture and nutrition.

reference.notes: A smooth, spreadable paste made from pork or beef liver, commonly sold in small cans in Filipino grocery stores. Reno is the most recognised brand. Rich, savoury, and slightly metallic in flavour. Used primarily as a thickener and flavour enhancer in Filipino stews, particularly caldereta, where it dissolves into the sauce and adds body, richness, and a deep savoury note. Can also be spread on bread or crackers. Store unopened in the pantry; refrigerate after opening and use within a week.
reference.purpose: Adds richness, body, and savoury depth to Filipino stews. Functions as both a thickener and flavour enhancer, particularly in caldereta where it gives the sauce its distinctive character.

reference.notes: In Australia, these are often the 'mildest' fresh chillies in the supermarket. They have a thicker wall than Thai chillies.
reference.purpose: Adds a mild, 'grassy' heat and crunch. It is perfect for people who want the flavor of chilli without the intense burn.
reference.storage: Keep in a bag in the fridge.
reference.usageTips: If you want zero heat, remove the white 'pith' (the ribs) from the inside. That is where 90% of the capsaicin lives.

reference.notes: These are generally much milder than the tiny 'Bird's Eye' chillies. They offer more 'fruitiness' and less 'burn.'
reference.purpose: Adds a medium heat and a beautiful vibrant red color. It is the most common 'everyday' chilli for stir-fries and pastas.
reference.storage: Keep in the fridge. For long-term storage, you can freeze them whole and grate them directly into your pan while frozen.
reference.usageTips: The heat is in the seeds and the white inner ribs. If you want the red color and the chilli flavor without the spice, simply scrape the seeds out before dicing.

reference.notes: Native to Australia! They have the hardest shell of any nut in the world, requiring 300 pounds of pressure per square inch to crack.
reference.purpose: The ultimate luxury nut. It provides an incredibly rich, buttery, and creamy texture to cookies and white chocolate desserts.
reference.storage: Keep in an airtight jar in the fridge. Their high oil content makes them go rancid quickly at room temperature.
reference.usageTips: Macadamias have the highest fat content of any nut. This means they can burn very quickly! If toasting them, watch them every second—they go from 'pale' to 'burnt' in a flash.

reference.notes: Malt powder is derived from sprouted barley and comes in diastatic and non-diastatic forms. - ** Non-diastatic malt powder adds sweetness and malt flavor without affecting rising. Use in breads, rolls, bagels, and other baked goods. - **Pairings:** Complements flour, yeast, honey, chocolate, nuts, and milk. - ** - **Substitutions:** Honey or brown sugar can replace malt powder for sweetness, though enzymatic activity will not be the same.
reference.purpose: Adds sweetness, enhances yeast activity, improves dough texture, and contributes rich crust color and malt aroma in baked goods.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to maintain potency.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Diastatic malt powder contains active enzymes that aid yeast fermentation and improve bread rise.

reference.notes: Mandarins are easier to peel and have less 'pith' than oranges. The 'Imperial' and 'Afourer' are the most popular varieties in Australia.
reference.purpose: Adds a sweet, floral, and very low-acid citrus burst. Perfect for kid-friendly snacks and bright fruit salads.
reference.storage: Store in a cool bowl on the counter or in the fridge if you want them to last longer than a week.
reference.usageTips: The zest of a mandarin is much more floral and 'perfumed' than an orange. Use a grater to add mandarin zest to your chocolate cake or muffin batter for a unique twist.

reference.notes: Mango is a tropical fruit with sweet, juicy flesh. - ** Can be pureed, sliced, or diced for desserts, smoothies, sauces, salsas, or salads. - **Pairings:** Complements coconut, lime, ginger, chili, yogurt, cream, berries, and other tropical fruits. - ** Peel before use. - **Substitutions:** Papaya or peach can be used as a substitute in texture and sweetness, though flavor differs.
reference.purpose: Adds sweet, tropical flavor, color, and moisture to desserts, beverages, and sauces, enhancing both taste and presentation.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store unripe mangoes at room temperature until ripe; refrigerate ripe mangoes for 3–5 days.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use ripe mangoes for best flavor.

reference.notes: Always look for '100% Pure Maple Syrup.' 'Maple-flavored' syrups are mostly corn syrup and chemicals with none of the complex flavor.
reference.purpose: Adds a unique, woody sweetness with hints of vanilla and caramel. It is thinner and cleaner-tasting than honey.
reference.storage: Once opened, you MUST store real maple syrup in the fridge. Because it is a natural product, it can develop mold if left in the pantry.
reference.usageTips: Maple syrup is a fantastic glaze for roasted vegetables like carrots or brussels sprouts. The sugar caramelizes into a savory-sweet crust.

reference.notes: Mars Bar is a chocolate bar consisting of chocolate, caramel, and nougat. - ** Can also be used as a topping or garnish. - **Pairings:** Complements chocolate, peanut butter, nuts, caramel, vanilla, and baked goods. - ** Best consumed before the expiration date for optimal texture and flavor. - **Substitutions:** Other chocolate bars with caramel and nougat (e.g., Snickers or Milky Way) can be used, though flavor balance may differ.
reference.purpose: Adds chocolate, caramel, and nougat flavor, sweetness, and texture to desserts, baked goods, and confections.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Can be chopped, melted, or folded into batter for brownies, cookies, cakes, or desserts.

reference.notes: A smooth, thick Italian cream cheese with a high fat content and a mild, slightly sweet flavour. Silky and spreadable straight from the refrigerator. Unlike regular cream cheese, mascarpone is made from cream rather than milk, giving it a richer, more luxurious texture. Used in both sweet and savoury dishes — essential in tiramisu, excellent in cheesecakes, and a wonderful addition to creamy pasta sauces and pie fillings where it melts into a velvety texture. Does not split when heated gently. Bring to room temperature before using for easier mixing. Store refrigerated and use within days of opening.
reference.purpose: Adds luxurious richness, creaminess, and a mild, sweet dairy flavour. Essential for authentic tiramisu. Used in both sweet desserts and savoury sauces for a silky texture.

reference.notes: Commercial mayo is an emulsion of oil, egg yolks, and vinegar. It is incredibly stable and won't split easily in cold dishes.
reference.purpose: Acts as a rich, creamy base for dressings and sandwiches. In baking, it can be used to add extreme moisture to chocolate cakes.
reference.storage: Must be refrigerated after opening. Do not freeze, as the emulsion will break and turn into oil.
reference.usageTips: The 'Chef's Secret': use mayonnaise instead of butter on the outside of your grilled cheese sandwich. It spreads easily and creates a more even, golden crust.

reference.notes: Mi Goreng means 'Fried Noodles.' Unlike Ramen, these are designed to be drained of their water before the seasonings are added.
reference.purpose: The essential base for Indonesian-style dry fried noodles. They offer a chewy, savory, and slightly sweet flavor profile.
reference.storage: Pantry stable.
reference.usageTips: The secret to the 'Mi Goreng' flavor is the Fried Shallots and the sweet Kecap Manis found in the little packets. Always add a squeeze of fresh lime to cut through the saltiness.

reference.notes: This is the classic Australian bacon cut. It gives you the best of both worlds: a meaty bite and a crispy, fatty finish.
reference.purpose: The 'Full-Flavor' bacon cut. It provides the lean 'eye' of the loin and the fatty 'tail' of the belly in one piece.
reference.storage: Keep cold and airtight.
reference.usageTips: If you find middle bacon too big for your pan, cut the 'tail' off and fry it separately. Use the crispy tail bits as a topping for salads or baked potatoes.

reference.notes: Milk chocolate contains dairy and more sugar than dark chocolate, making it much more popular in kid-friendly baking.
reference.purpose: A sweet, creamy mix-in for muffins and cookies. They are designed to hold their shape and provide a soft, melty bite.
reference.storage: Store in a cool dark place.
reference.usageTips: To prevent choc bits from sinking to the bottom of your muffins, toss them in a little bit of the recipe's flour before folding them into the batter.

reference.notes: In Australia, full-cream milk must have a minimum fat content of 3.2%. This fat is what provides the 'creamy' mouthfeel in Béchamel and Custards.
reference.purpose: Provides the richest liquid base for baking, sauces, and drinks. It adds fat, protein, and natural sugar (lactose).
reference.storage: Fridge.
reference.usageTips: If your sauce keeps burning to the bottom of the pan, you are using the heat too high. Milk has natural sugars that 'scorch' easily. Always heat milk-based sauces on a medium-low flame and stir constantly.

reference.notes: Refer to Milk Powder entry in main inventory.
reference.purpose: High-fat powder adds richness, creaminess, and mouthfeel. Enhances texture, browning, and moisture retention in doughs and batters.
reference.storage: Store in an airtight container, away from moisture and heat for best shelf life.

reference.notes: Because the fat has been removed, skim milk powder adds the protein and sugar (lactose) of milk without making the dough greasy.
reference.purpose: Acts as a 'dough conditioner' in bread making. It improves the crust color and creates a softer, more tender crumb.
reference.storage: Store in an airtight container. It can absorb moisture and turn into a rock if left open.
reference.usageTips: Use skim milk powder in your Bread Machine recipes to get a more golden-brown crust. The lactose sugar in the powder caramelizes beautifully in the heat of the oven.

reference.notes: Skim milk is essentially full-cream milk with the cream (fat) spun out. It is higher in calcium per cup than full-cream milk.
reference.purpose: Provides a lighter liquid base for coffee, cereal, and batters where you want less fat than full-cream milk.
reference.storage: Fridge.
reference.usageTips: In baking, skim milk will produce a slightly less rich and less 'tender' result than full-cream. If you only have skim, you can add a teaspoon of butter to compensate for the lost fat.

reference.notes: Mint leaves are aromatic herbs used fresh in a variety of dishes. - ** Can be finely chopped, torn, or blended. Freezing preserves flavor but may reduce texture. - **Pairings:** Complements yogurt, lemon, lime, coriander, lamb, peas, chocolate, and fruits. - ** Can also be frozen or dried for longer storage. - **Substitutions:** Spearmint or peppermint can replace fresh mint, though flavor intensity differs.
reference.purpose: Adds fresh, cool, and aromatic flavor to curries, salads, sauces, drinks, desserts, and raita.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store fresh leaves in a sealed container or wrapped in a damp paper towel in the refrigerator for up to a week.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use fresh leaves for garnishing, sauces, chutneys, salads, or in curries and raita.

reference.notes: Classic mint sauce is made from finely chopped mint leaves, sugar, and malt vinegar. It 'brightens' the palate between bites of heavy meat.
reference.purpose: The traditional partner for roast lamb. It provides a sharp, vinegar-based acidity that cuts through the rich lamb fat.
reference.storage: Refrigerate after opening.
reference.usageTips: Add a teaspoon of store-bought mint sauce to your next pea soup or over buttered carrots for an instant flavor upgrade.

reference.notes: Mirin is a traditional Japanese sweet rice wine with low alcohol content. - ** Adds subtle sweetness and depth without overpowering other flavors. - **Pairings:** Complements soy sauce, sake, dashi, ginger, garlic, and sesame. - ** Once opened, refrigerate and use within a few months for best flavor. - **Substitutions:** Can be replaced with a mixture of sake and sugar or a mild rice vinegar with sugar if unavailable, though flavor will differ.
reference.purpose: Provides sweetness, umami, and a glossy finish to sauces, marinades, and stir-fries. Balances salty and savory elements, enhances caramelization, and softens strong flavors in Japanese and Asian dishes.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dark place.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Commonly used in teriyaki, sukiyaki, stir-fries, glazes, and marinades.

reference.notes: Miso is made from fermented soybeans. 'White' miso is mild and sweet; 'Red' miso is strong and very salty.
reference.purpose: Adds an incredible 'fifth taste' (Umami). It provides a salty, fermented depth that makes soups and marinades taste professionally made.
reference.storage: Must be kept in the fridge. It will stay good for up to a year.
reference.usageTips: Never boil miso! High heat kills the healthy probiotics and destroys its delicate flavor. Always whisk it into your soup at the very end, after you've turned off the stove.

reference.notes: Mixed herbs are a dried blend of multiple herbs; exact composition varies by brand but often includes parsley, thyme, marjoram, rosemary, and oregano. - ** Adjust quantity to taste. Can be added during cooking or as a finishing garnish. - **Pairings:** Complements meats, poultry, vegetables, grains, and sauces. - ** - **Substitutions:** Any single dried herb or combination of herbs can be used, though flavor balance may differ.
reference.purpose: Adds versatile aromatic flavor to a wide variety of dishes, enhancing both taste and aroma without overpowering other ingredients.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dark place in an airtight container to maintain flavor and aroma.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use to season soups, stews, sauces, roasted vegetables, and general dishes.

reference.notes: In Australia/UK, this is a specific blend of Cinnamon, Nutmeg, Allspice, and Cloves. It is different from Gingerbread spice.
reference.purpose: The classic 'Christmas in a jar' flavor. It adds warm, sweet, and woody notes to fruit cakes, buns, and puddings.
reference.storage: Keep in a cool, dark place.
reference.usageTips: Add a teaspoon to your apple pie filling or even your morning oats to instantly elevate the flavor profile.

reference.notes: Molasses is a by-product of sugar refining, dark, thick, and robust in flavor. - ** Blackstrap molasses is stronger and more bitter than light or dark molasses; adjust quantity to taste. - **Pairings:** Complements spices like ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, citrus, chocolate, and nuts. - ** Refrigeration can extend shelf life. - **Substitutions:** Light or dark molasses, honey, or brown sugar can replace molasses, though flavor intensity will differ.
reference.purpose: Adds deep, robust sweetness, dark color, and moisture to baked goods and sauces. Enhances flavor complexity and richness, particularly in dense breads, spiced desserts, and savory glazes.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place in a sealed container to prevent crystallization.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Commonly used in gingerbread, dark breads, baked beans, barbecue sauces, and marinades.

reference.notes: Usually based on 'Ras el Hanout,' a blend that can contain up to 30 spices, including cinnamon, cumin, ginger, and turmeric.
reference.purpose: Adds a warm, aromatic, and exotic depth. It is savory and sweet without being 'hot.'
reference.storage: Airtight jar.
reference.usageTips: This is the best seasoning for roasted pumpkin or sweet potato. The cinnamon and ginger in the blend highlight the natural sugars in the vegetables perfectly.

reference.notes: A mild, white Italian cheese with a soft, elastic texture and excellent melting properties. Available fresh (packed in whey or water) or as low-moisture block cheese. Fresh mozzarella is soft, moist, and delicate — best torn and used in salads or on pizza where it melts into creamy pools. Low-moisture mozzarella is firmer, grates easily, and gives the classic stretchy, golden melt on pizzas, lasagne, and baked pasta dishes. For lasagne, use low-moisture mozzarella for even melting and browning. Store fresh mozzarella in its liquid; block mozzarella wrapped in the refrigerator.
reference.purpose: Provides mild, creamy flavour, excellent stretch, and golden browning when melted. Essential for pizza, lasagne, and baked pasta dishes where a smooth, even melt is desired.

reference.notes: Mozzarella has a mild, milky flavor, which is why it is often blended with sharper cheeses like Cheddar or Parmesan for more taste.
reference.purpose: The king of melting cheeses. It provides the iconic 'stretch' and golden bubbles on pizzas and pasta bakes.
reference.storage: Keep well wrapped. If you have extra, grated mozzarella freezes perfectly for months.
reference.usageTips: For the best pizza stretch, use 'Low Moisture' mozzarella (the block kind) and grate it yourself. Fresh mozzarella (the balls in water) is too wet for most home ovens.

reference.notes: Mushrooms are versatile fungi used fresh or cooked in a variety of dishes. - **Swiss Brown / Chestnut Mushrooms:** Firmer, slightly nuttier, holds shape well; ideal for sauces, roasting, or sautés. - **Button / White Mushrooms:** Mild flavor, versatile; good raw in salads or cooked in a wide range of dishes. - **Flat / Large / Portobello Mushrooms:** Meaty texture and earthy flavor; perfect for grilling, stuffing, or hearty recipes. - ** Cooking intensifies umami. Clean gently with a damp cloth; avoid soaking. - ** Use promptly for best texture and flavor. - **Substitutions:** Other edible mushrooms like shiitake, oyster, or cremini can be used depending on texture and flavor needs.
reference.purpose: Adds umami, moisture, texture, and depth of flavor; versatile in sautés, sauces, soups, salads, roasting, grilling, and baking.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place, ideally in a paper bag in the refrigerator.
reference.usageTips: Usage Tips:** All mushrooms are Agaricus bisporus.

reference.notes: All mustards are made from the seeds of the brassica plant. The lighter the seed, the milder the mustard.
reference.purpose: The ultimate sharp seasoning. It adds acidity, heat, and acts as a binder for marinades and dressings.
reference.storage: Refrigerate after opening.
reference.usageTips: Did You Know? Mustard is a natural thickener. If your pan sauce is a bit thin, whisk in a teaspoon of smooth mustard—it will thicken the sauce and add flavor at the same time.

reference.notes: Mustard seeds come in black, brown, and yellow varieties, each with distinct flavor and heat levels. - ** Can also be ground for spice blends or pastes. - **Pairings:** Complements cumin, coriander, curry leaves, turmeric, garlic, ginger, and dals. - ** Grind just before use for maximum aroma. - **Substitutions:** Yellow mustard seeds can be used in place of black or brown seeds, though heat and flavor intensity will vary.
reference.purpose: Adds pungent, nutty flavor and aroma. Pops when tempered in hot oil to enhance curries, dals, pickles, and other Indian dishes.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place to preserve potency and flavor.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Whole seeds are preferred for tempering in hot oil (tadka) to release aroma and nutty flavor.

reference.notes: Naan is a leavened, oven-baked flatbread traditionally cooked in a tandoor oven, popular in Indian and South Asian cuisine. - **Store-Bought Naan:** Available fresh or frozen. Heat in a dry pan, under a grill, or in a 180°C oven wrapped in foil for 5 minutes. - **Garlic Naan:** Topped with butter, minced garlic, and sometimes coriander; ideal alongside curries. - **Uses:** Primary accompaniment to curries, dips, and sauces. Can be used as a pizza base or wrap. - **Roti / Chapati:** Unleavened whole wheat flatbreads; thinner and less fluffy than naan but similarly versatile. - **Pita Bread:** Greek-style flatbread with a pocket; excellent for fillings and alongside dips.
reference.purpose: Serves as a flavourful, absorbent accompaniment to curries, stews, and dips. Adds texture contrast and provides a vehicle for sauces and toppings.

reference.notes: Unlike 'Essence' (which is synthetic), 'Extract' is made by soaking real vanilla beans in alcohol. It contains hundreds of flavor compounds that essence simply cannot replicate.
reference.purpose: Provides the purest, most complex vanilla flavor. It acts as the 'soul' of high-quality baking, balancing sweetness and eggs.
reference.storage: Store in a cool, dark place. Real extract actually improves with age, much like a fine wine.
reference.usageTips: Because it contains alcohol, the smell is very strong when you open the bottle. However, the alcohol burns off in the oven, leaving behind only the sweet, floral aroma of the beans.

reference.notes: Natural yoghurt contains 'live cultures.' It is less processed and less thick than Greek yoghurt, making it easier to pour and stir into batters.
reference.purpose: Adds a cooling, creamy tang. It acts as a meat tenderizer in marinades and a moisture-booster in cakes.
reference.storage: Fridge. Do not eat if the tub is 'bloated' or smells like yeast.
reference.usageTips: If you are using yoghurt in a hot curry, whisk it with 1 teaspoon of cornflour first. This prevents the yoghurt from curdling and turning into white 'dots' when it hits the hot sauce.

reference.notes: Nectarines are firm, juicy stone fruits with smooth edible skin. - ** Can be poached, roasted, or grilled to intensify flavor. - **Pairings:** Complements berries, stone fruits, cream, custard, almonds, cinnamon, and honey. - ** Handle gently to avoid bruising. - **Substitutions:** Peaches can be used as a similar alternative with slightly fuzzier texture.
reference.purpose: Adds natural sweetness, aroma, and moisture. Enhances texture, flavor balance, and visual appeal in desserts and baked goods.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store at room temperature until ripe, then refrigerate to extend freshness.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use fresh, sliced, or diced in tarts, pies, crisps, cakes, salads, or as a snack.

reference.notes: Pronounced like the French city 'Nee-se.' These are simple sugar-dusted biscuits that have been a pantry staple since the late 1800s.
reference.purpose: Provides a light, coconut-flavored crunch. Excellent as a subtle base for lemon or fruit-based cheesecakes.
reference.storage: Airtight container.
reference.usageTips: Because they are thinner and lighter than digestive biscuits, they make a more delicate crust that doesn't overpower light fruit fillings.

reference.notes: Small matte-black seeds with a slightly bitter, peppery flavour and subtle onion, oregano, and nutty notes. Popular in Middle Eastern, Indian, and North African cuisines; sprinkled on flatbreads, naan, pastries, pickles, vegetables, and legumes. In Filipino cooking, less traditional but useful for bread, rice dishes, and spice blends. Toast briefly in a dry pan to release flavour, but avoid burning.
reference.purpose: Adds a distinctively bitter, peppery, and slightly onion-like flavour as a topping or seasoning. Primarily used as a visual and aromatic garnish on flatbreads, naan, Turkish bread, and pastries. Lightly toasted seeds enhance flavour; used whole rather than ground in most applications.
reference.storage: Store in an airtight container away from heat and light for up to 2–3 years.
reference.usageTips: Commonly used whole or lightly toasted to enhance aroma.

reference.notes: Nutella is a sweet chocolate-hazelnut spread. - ** - **Pairings:** Complements bread, pastries, crepes, bananas, strawberries, and other fruits. - ** Keep tightly sealed to maintain flavor. - **Substitutions:** Other chocolate-hazelnut spreads or homemade versions can be used, though flavor and texture may differ.
reference.purpose: Adds chocolate-hazelnut flavor, sweetness, and creaminess to spreads, baked goods, desserts, and toppings.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place; do not refrigerate as it can harden.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use as a spread on bread, toast, or pancakes; incorporate into baking, fillings, frostings, or as a topping for desserts.

reference.notes: EVOO has a low smoke point (approx 190°C), meaning it can smoke and lose flavor if used for high-heat wok cooking or deep frying.
reference.purpose: A foundational cooking fat. Extra Virgin (EVOO) is for flavor and dressings; 'Light' or 'Pure' is for general frying.
reference.storage: Keep in a cool, dark cupboard. Do not store it next to the stove where it gets hot.
reference.usageTips: Buy your olive oil in dark bottles or tins. Light and heat are the enemies of oil; they make it go rancid and taste like 'old crayons.'

reference.notes: Onions are versatile aromatic vegetables used as a base in cooking. - ** - **Pairings:** Complements garlic, herbs, tomatoes, meats, and other vegetables. - ** Avoid refrigeration for whole onions; sliced onions should be refrigerated and used promptly. - **Substitutions:** Shallots or leeks can replace onions in certain recipes for milder flavor or aroma.
reference.purpose: Provides foundational flavor and aromatic base for sauces, soups, stews, sautés, and roasted dishes; enhances sweetness, depth, and complexity.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry, well-ventilated place.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Brown onions provide depth and richness in soups, stews, and braises; white onions are sharper and ideal for sautés, sauces, and raw preparations; Spanish onions are sweeter, perfect for caramelizing or salads.

reference.notes: It is a key ingredient in 'Hidden Valley' style ranch dressings and is the secret to getting a 'meaty' flavor in vegetarian cooking.
reference.purpose: Adds a savory, 'umami' sweetness and depth to savory dishes without the texture or moisture of fresh onions.
reference.storage: Keep the lid tight! Like garlic powder, it will absorb moisture from the air and turn solid if left open.
reference.usageTips: Mix onion powder into your flour coating when frying chicken or fish for an instant flavor upgrade that fresh onions can't provide.

reference.notes: Orange zest is the finely grated outer peel of oranges, providing concentrated citrus aroma and flavor. - ** Avoid the bitter white pith. - **Pairings:** Complements chocolate, nuts, berries, cream, yogurt, and citrus-based desserts. - ** - **Substitutions:** Lemon or lime zest can be used for different citrus notes, though flavor will vary.
reference.purpose: Adds bright, aromatic citrus flavor and fragrance to sweet and savory dishes, enhancing both taste and aroma.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place; can also be frozen for long-term use.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use in baking, desserts, marinades, sauces, dressings, and beverages.

reference.notes: Refer to Orange entry for full details.
reference.purpose: Adds bright, aromatic citrus flavor and fragrance.

reference.notes: Oregano is a fragrant herb - **Usage:** Dried oregano is more potent than fresh; add early in cooking to allow flavor to bloom. Fresh oregano can be added toward the end for bright, aromatic notes. - **Pairings:** Complements tomato, garlic, olive oil, cheeses, meats, and vegetables. - ** - **Substitutions:** Marjoram or thyme can be used for a milder, similar flavor.
reference.purpose: Adds warm, aromatic, slightly bitter and peppery herb flavor to sauces, roasted vegetables, meats, and Mediterranean dishes.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store dried oregano in an airtight container in a cool, dark place; fresh oregano can be refrigerated or frozen.
reference.usageTips: commonly used in Mediterranean and tomato-based dishes.

reference.notes: The dark color comes from 'Dutch-processed' cocoa, which is alkaline and has a very distinct, mellow chocolate flavor.
reference.purpose: The gold standard for 'Cookies & Cream' desserts. They provide a dark, cocoa-rich crunch and a creamy center.
reference.storage: Store in an airtight container to keep them snappy.
reference.usageTips: To make an instant cheesecake base, crush a whole pack of Oreos (filling and all) in a food processor and mix with 60g of melted butter. It is much tastier than a standard biscuit base!

reference.notes: A thick, dark brown sauce made from oyster extracts, sugar, salt, and cornstarch. Rich, savoury, and slightly sweet with a distinct umami depth that is not fishy. Used extensively in Chinese and Southeast Asian stir-fries, noodle dishes, and as a finishing sauce for vegetables. Adds both flavour and a glossy sheen. A small amount goes a long way. Stir into dishes towards the end of cooking to preserve its flavour.
reference.purpose: Adds rich umami depth, subtle sweetness, and a glossy finish to stir-fries, noodle dishes, and vegetable preparations. Provides the savoury backbone in dishes like Filipino pancit canton and Mongolian beef.
reference.storage: Store in the refrigerator after opening.

reference.notes: Refer to Seafood entry for full details.
reference.purpose: Best served freshly shucked. When used in cooking (e.g., Carpetbag steak), lightly pan-fry or add at the last minute.

reference.notes: Paprika is a ground spice made from dried red peppers, ranging from sweet to hot and smoked varieties. - ** Ideal for sauces, stews, rubs, marinades, soups, and roasted vegetables. Toast lightly in a dry pan or oil to release aroma. - **Pairings:** Complements garlic, onion, meats, potatoes, eggs, beans, and other vegetables. - ** - **Substitutions:** Chili powder or cayenne can be used for heat; smoked paprika
reference.purpose: Provides mild heat, vibrant red colour, and aromatic depth; enhances visual appeal and balances flavours in curries, sauces, meats, and vegetable dishes.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place to preserve colour, aroma, and flavor.
reference.substitutes: can be substituted with chipotle powder for smoky notes.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use sweet, hot, or smoked paprika depending on desired flavor.

reference.notes: A hard, granular Italian cheese made from cow's milk, aged for 12-36 months. Intensely savoury, nutty, and slightly crystalline with a granular texture that melts into sauces. A little goes a long way due to its concentrated flavour. Grate fresh from the block for the best flavour and melting quality — pre-grated Parmesan contains anti-caking agents and loses its aromatic oils quickly. Use in pasta, risotto, pesto, sauces, and as a finishing cheese. The rind can be added to soups and stocks for extra depth. Store wrapped in wax paper or cheese paper in the refrigerator.
reference.purpose: Adds intense umami, saltiness, and nutty depth to pasta, sauces, pesto, and baked dishes. Functions as both a cooking ingredient and a finishing cheese. A cornerstone of Italian cuisine.

reference.notes: Parmesan is a hard, aged cheese. In Australia, this usually refers to a 'Grana' style cheese aged for at least 12 months.
reference.purpose: Adds an intense savory 'Umami' punch and a salty, nutty depth to pasta, risotto, and bakes.
reference.storage: Wrap in wax paper or foil rather than plastic wrap. If it gets a small spot of surface mold, just scrape it off; the cheese is too dry for the mold to penetrate deep.
reference.usageTips: Don't throw away the hard rind! Keep it in a bag in the freezer and drop it into your next Minestrone or Bolognese while it simmers. The rind will melt slightly, adding a massive boost of flavor to the sauce.

reference.notes: Shaved parmesan stays firm and offers a satisfying 'snap' when eaten, making it a great textural element.
reference.purpose: Used primarily as a finishing touch for salads and plated pastas. Provides larger 'hits' of salty flavor than grated cheese.
reference.storage: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge. Because of the high surface area, shaved cheese dries out much faster than a block.
reference.usageTips: Toss shaved parmesan into a rocket and pear salad just before serving. The wide ribbons look beautiful and ensure you get a perfect balance of cheese in every forkful.

reference.notes: Parsley is a fresh herb used for flavoring, garnishing, and enhancing baked goods. - ** Curly parsley is best for garnish and visual appeal. - **Pairings:** Complements garlic, lemon, butter, eggs, vegetables, and meats. - ** - **Substitutions:** Cilantro or chervil can be used for a similar fresh, green note depending on the dish.
reference.purpose: Adds fresh, mild, slightly peppery flavor and bright green color to breads, pastries, sauces, and savory dishes.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store fresh parsley wrapped in damp paper towel in the refrigerator or freeze chopped for long-term use.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use flat-leaf (Italian) parsley for stronger flavor in breads, savory pastries, sauces, and sautés.

reference.notes: Passata is made from tomatoes that have been pureed and strained to remove all seeds and skins. It is much thicker than juice but thinner than paste.
reference.purpose: The base for smooth Italian pasta sauces and soups. It is tomato sauce in its purest, most liquid form.
reference.storage: Transfer to a jar after opening. It only lasts about 4-5 days in the fridge before it starts to ferment.
reference.usageTips: Passata is uncooked! Always simmer it for at least 15-20 minutes with garlic and herbs to cook off the 'raw' tomato taste and develop sweetness.

reference.notes: Passionfruit is a tropical fruit with aromatic pulp and crunchy seeds. - ** Can be used fresh or in purees. - **Pairings:** Complements cream, custards, chocolate, citrus, and tropical fruits. - ** Pulp can be frozen for later use. - **Substitutions:** Mango or kiwi can provide a similar tropical tang in certain recipes.
reference.purpose: Adds bright, tart, and aromatic tropical flavor; enhances aroma, acidity, and visual appeal in sweet and dessert dishes.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store whole fruit at room temperature until ripe; refrigerate after cutting.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Scoop out pulp and seeds for use in desserts, tarts, pavlovas, sauces, drinks, and marinades.

reference.notes: Pastries are dough-based products used for sweet or savory dishes, with different types providing varied textures. - **Puff (Flaky Pastry):** Keep cold before baking and handle gently to maintain light, flaky layers. Ideal for tarts, vol-au-vents, pies, and savory turnovers. - **Shortcrust (Short Pastry):** Mix minimally to ensure a tender, crumbly texture. Chill before rolling; excellent for pie bases, quiches, and tarts. - ** Both can be blind-baked or filled as required. - ** - **Substitutions:** Puff can substitute for shortcrust in some recipes for a flakier texture; shortcrust can be used when a sturdy base is needed.
reference.purpose: Provides structure, texture, and flavor for sweet or savory dishes; puff pastry gives airy, flaky layers, while shortcrust provides tender, crisp bases.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store refrigerated or frozen; thaw chilled before use to preserve texture.
reference.usageTips: Usage Tips:** Use appropriate pastry type depending on desired texture and dish.

reference.notes: Peaches are juicy, aromatic fruits with sweet flesh and edible skin. - ** Peel optional. Slice, dice, or purée for tarts, pies, cobblers, jams, compotes, or desserts. Can also be roasted, poached, or grilled to intensify flavor. - **Pairings:** Complements cream, yogurt, nuts, spices like cinnamon or nutmeg, and other fruits. - ** Can be frozen or canned for longer storage. - **Substitutions:** Nectarine or apricot can be used as similar-tasting alternatives.
reference.purpose: Adds natural sweetness, juiciness, aroma, and color to desserts; enhances texture, moisture, and visual appeal.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store unripe peaches at room temperature to ripen; refrigerate ripe peaches and use within a few days.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use ripe but firm fruit.

reference.notes: Tinned peaches are a fantastic pantry staple because they are consistently sweet and soft, unlike fresh peaches which can sometimes be mealy or under-ripe.
reference.purpose: Provides a soft, honey-like sweetness and a vibrant orange color to desserts and breakfast bowls.
reference.storage: Refrigerate in a sealed container once opened.
reference.usageTips: If you are using these in a tart, pat them dry with a paper towel first. Excess juice can make the bottom of your pastry soggy.

reference.notes: Store raw peanuts in a cool, dry place for up to 3 months, or refrigerate/freeze for longer storage. Roasted peanuts should be kept in an airtight container to maintain freshness. Can be eaten raw, roasted, boiled, or ground into peanut butter. Common allergen—always check with guests before serving. Available shelled or unshelled, salted or unsalted, and in various forms (whole, halved, chopped, or ground). To enhance flavor, toast in a dry skillet or oven before use. Remove skins after roasting by rubbing in a clean towel if desired. Used in both sweet and savory dishes across many cuisines.
reference.purpose: Provides protein, healthy fats, and a rich, nutty flavor. Used in cooking, baking, snacking, and as a base for sauces (like satay), spreads (peanut butter), and confections. Popular in Asian, African, and American cuisines.

reference.notes: Did You Know? It takes about 540 peanuts to make one 375g jar of peanut butter!
reference.purpose: Adds a rich, salty, and nutty protein base. It acts as a thickener for savory sauces (Satay) and a binder for cookies.
reference.storage: Store in the pantry. If you buy 'Natural' peanut butter, store it upside down—this helps the oil redistribute through the jar so you don't end up with a dry lump at the bottom.
reference.usageTips: If you are making a savory Asian sauce, use 'Crunchy' peanut butter. The tiny bits of nut add a professional texture that smooth peanut butter lacks.

reference.notes: Peanut oil doesn't absorb the flavors of the food cooked in it, which means you can reuse the oil for frying several times.
reference.purpose: The gold standard for deep-frying and high-heat wok cooking. It has a high smoke point and a neutral, slightly nutty finish.
reference.storage: Store in a cool, dark place. If the oil looks cloudy or smells like 'old paint,' it has gone rancid and should be tossed.
reference.usageTips: It is the best oil for authentic 'Crispy Skin' chicken or fish. It can handle the high heat required to blister the skin without burning.

reference.notes: Pears are sweet, juicy fruits with a delicate aroma and soft flesh. - ** Peel optional. Ideal for poaching, baking in tarts, crumbles, cakes, or making compotes and preserves. Choose variety based on sweetness, firmness, and texture. - **Pairings:** Complements spices such as cinnamon, nutmeg, and cardamom, as well as apples, citrus, nuts, and cream. - ** Can be canned or frozen for longer storage. - **Substitutions:** Apples or quince can be used for similar texture and sweetness in recipes.
reference.purpose: Adds natural sweetness, moisture, tender texture, and subtle fragrance to desserts; enhances flavors and complements spices and other fruits.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store unripe pears at room temperature to ripen; refrigerate ripe pears to extend freshness.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use ripe but firm pears.

reference.notes: Pecans are sweet, buttery nuts - **Usage:** Chop, toast, or use whole in pies, cookies, cakes, granola, and salads. Toasting enhances aroma and flavor. - **Pairings:** Complements chocolate, caramel, brown sugar, apples, pears, and spices like cinnamon and nutmeg. - ** - **Substitutions:** Walnuts can be used in recipes as a similar-textured nut with slightly different flavor.
reference.purpose: Adds crunch, buttery richness, and sweet nutty flavor to baked goods, desserts, and salads.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place; refrigerate or freeze for longer shelf life.
reference.usageTips: commonly used in baking and desserts.

reference.notes: Pecans are native to North America. They have a very high oil content, which is why they taste so rich and 'melt-in-the-mouth.'
reference.purpose: Adds a sweet, buttery crunch. They are softer and richer than walnuts, making them the ultimate choice for pies and brownies.
reference.storage: Store in the freezer if you don't use them often. The high fat content makes them go rancid (tasting like soap) very quickly at room temperature.
reference.usageTips: Always toast pecans before using! 5 minutes in a 180°C oven transforms them from 'soft and bland' to 'dark, crispy, and aromatic.'

reference.notes: These are usually 'Plum' or 'San Marzano' style tomatoes. Because they are whole, they retain more of their natural sweetness than pre-crushed tomatoes.
reference.purpose: The gold standard for long-simmered Italian sauces. They provide a rustic texture that you can control.
reference.storage: Pantry.
reference.usageTips: Don't chop them with a knife! Tip the can into a bowl and crush the tomatoes with your hands. This gives you a variety of chunky and smooth pieces, which is the secret to a 'restaurant-style' rustic sauce.

reference.notes: Pepper comes in several forms, each with distinct aroma and heat. - **Black Peppercorns:** Sharp, pungent flavour; best freshly cracked for maximum aroma. Ideal for stocks, sauces, meats, and slow-cooked dishes. - **Green Peppercorns:** Milder, slightly fruity; often used in cream sauces, pickles, and light dishes. Can be used fresh, frozen, or brined. - **Ground Pepper:** Convenient form; black or white varieties. Enhances other flavours and adds mild heat. Use fresh-ground for best aroma. - **Tips:** Toast whole peppercorns lightly to enhance flavour before grinding. Adjust quantity depending on heat preference. Store whole or ground pepper in airtight containers away from heat and light. - **White Pepper:** Milder and less pungent than black; used in white sauces, light-coloured dishes, and Asian cooking where black specks are undesirable.
reference.purpose: Adds heat, aroma, and a peppery bite to a wide range of dishes. Enhances savoury flavours in sauces, soups, stocks, meats, and vegetables.

reference.notes: Pepperoni is a cured dry sausage. When baked, the edges crisp up into 'cups' that trap the delicious spicy oils.
reference.purpose: Adds a salty, spicy, and smoky fat content. It is the most iconic topping for a savory pizza.
reference.storage: Keep refrigerated.
reference.usageTips: If you find pepperoni too greasy on your pizza, lay the slices on a paper towel and microwave them for 15 seconds before putting them on the dough—this removes the excess 'orange' oil.

reference.notes: Cream cheese is a soft, mild-tasting fresh cheese. - ** Can be whipped or folded into batters. - **Pairings:** Complements sugar, citrus, chocolate, berries, herbs, and smoked salmon. - ** Can be frozen for longer storage but may affect texture. - **Substitutions:** Mascarpone, ricotta, or Greek yogurt can replace cream cheese in some recipes with texture adjustments.
reference.purpose: Adds creamy texture, mild tang, and richness to desserts, frostings, and spreads.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store refrigerated; consume by the use-by date.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Best used at room temperature for smooth mixing in cheesecakes, frostings, dips, and spreads.

reference.notes: The pickling process mellows the raw 'grassy' heat of the chilli and replaces it with a tangy 'zing.'
reference.purpose: Provides a bright, vinegary heat. They are the 'acid' element that balances out heavy, cheesy dishes like nachos.
reference.storage: Keep in the fridge once opened. Ensure they stay submerged in the vinegar liquid to prevent mold.
reference.usageTips: Chop these up and mix them into your corn muffin batter or even into a tuna sandwich filling for a sudden burst of flavor.

reference.notes: Pine nuts are the edible seeds of pine trees, harvested from the cones. Small, elongated, and cream-coloured. - **Flavour:** Mild, sweet, and buttery with a slight resinous note. - **Toasting:** Dry-toast in a pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, until golden — 3–4 minutes. Watch closely as they can burn very quickly. Toasting deepens flavour significantly. - **Common Uses:** Essential in traditional pesto, added to salads, pasta, pilafs, and baked goods. Used as garnish on dips and in Middle Eastern cooking. - ** Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 month, or freeze for up to 6 months.
reference.purpose: Adds buttery, slightly sweet flavour and tender crunch. Essential in pesto; used to enrich pasta dishes, salads, and grain dishes. Toasted pine nuts provide a flavour and texture contrast as garnish.
reference.storage: Storage:** High oil content makes pine nuts perishable.

reference.notes: Pineapple is a tropical fruit with sweet, tart, and juicy flesh. - ** Drain syrup if using canned and not needed. Tidbits are small, uniform pieces ideal for baking, salads, or toppings. Can be chopped, juiced, or folded into batters. - **Pairings:** Complements coconut, cream, rum, brown sugar, ginger, and other tropical fruits. - ** Canned pineapple can be stored unopened at room temperature; refrigerate after opening. - **Substitutions:** Mango, papaya, or peaches can be used for similar tropical sweetness in some recipes.
reference.purpose: Adds natural sweetness, acidity, moisture, tropical aroma, and vibrant flavor to both sweet and savory dishes.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store fresh pineapple in a cool place until cut; refrigerate cut fruit and consume within a few days.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use fresh, canned, crushed, sliced, tidbits, or chunks depending on recipe.

reference.notes: Chunks are sturdier than 'Crushed' pineapple, meaning they won't disappear into a sauce or batter.
reference.purpose: Adds bite-sized tropical sweetness and moisture. Ideal for stir-fries and fruit salads.
reference.storage: Move to a sealed container once opened.
reference.usageTips: When making 'Sweet and Sour Pork,' add the pineapple chunks at the very end of the cook. You want them to be hot, but you don't want them to lose their 'snap' and turn into mush.

reference.notes: Refer to Juice entry in main inventory.
reference.purpose: Balances salty, sweet, and sour elements in savory sauces, marinades, and tropical desserts. Adds tropical aroma and slight tang.

reference.notes: Often interchangeably sold with 'Chunks' or 'Tidbits' depending on the brand.
reference.purpose: A versatile, mid-sized fruit cut. Perfect for toppings and snacking.
reference.storage: Fridge.
reference.usageTips: If you are making Hawaiian-style skewers, use these pieces. They are the perfect size to sit on a toothpick alongside a piece of ham and a cherry tomato.

reference.notes: Identical in flavor to slices, but cut into perfect circles. The hole in the middle is where the tough core was removed.
reference.purpose: Provides a consistent, round fruit element. Perfect for presentation on top of hams or inside burgers.
reference.storage: Move to a glass container once opened.
reference.usageTips: Use these to top a gammon steak or a thick pork chop. The round shape perfectly fits the top of the meat, ensuring you get a hit of sweet pineapple in every single bite.

reference.notes: Slices are perfect for when you want a 'uniform' piece of fruit in every bite.
reference.purpose: The classic topping for 'Aussie' burgers and Hawaiian pizzas. They provide a sweet, juicy contrast to salty meats.
reference.storage: Refrigerate in a separate container once opened.
reference.usageTips: For a 'Gourmet Burger,' grill the pineapple slice on a hot pan for 1 minute per side until it has dark char marks. The heat caramelizes the sugar and makes it much more savory.

reference.notes: Bred in Australia in the 1970s. It was the first apple in the world to be trademarked!
reference.purpose: Australia's favorite eating apple. It provides a sweet-tart 'fizz' flavor and a very crisp, crunchy texture.
reference.storage: Fridge.
reference.usageTips: Because they are so firm, Pink Ladies hold their shape exceptionally well when sliced thin for salads or used as a topping for tarts. They don't turn to mush as easily as other red apples.

reference.notes: Known as the 'Smiling Nut.' They are one of the lowest-calorie nuts and are packed with antioxidants.
reference.purpose: Mainly used for their stunning lime-green color and their unique, slightly floral nuttiness.
reference.storage: Airtight jar.
reference.usageTips: If using for decoration, look for 'Slivered' or 'Raw' pistachios. The bright green color is only visible if the thin purple skin is removed—you can do this by blanching them in boiling water for 1 minute.

reference.notes: Also called 'All-Purpose' flour. It doesn't contain any raising agents, so you have complete control over the rise.
reference.purpose: The 'all-purpose' workhorse. It has a medium protein level suitable for cookies, pancakes, and general cooking.
reference.storage: Store in a cool, dry place. Sift before use if your flour looks lumpy.
reference.usageTips: If a recipe calls for Self-Raising flour and you only have Plain, add 1.5 teaspoons of baking powder and half a teaspoon of salt for every cup of flour.

reference.notes: Plums are sweet-tart stone fruits with smooth skin and juicy flesh. - ** Ideal for baking in tarts, cakes, crumbles, or stewing for sauces, jams, and preserves. Skin adds color and slight tartness. - **Pairings:** Complements cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, almonds, citrus, and other stone fruits. - ** Can be frozen or canned for long-term storage. - **Substitutions:** Peaches, nectarines, or apricots can be used for similar texture and sweetness.
reference.purpose: Adds balanced sweetness, acidity, moisture, and vibrant color; enhances flavor and visual appeal in desserts and preserves.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store unripe plums at room temperature to ripen; refrigerate ripe plums and use within a few days.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use ripe but firm plums; pit removed.

reference.notes: Plum jam is naturally higher in acid than strawberry jam, making it a better choice for balancing very sweet desserts.
reference.purpose: Adds a deep, tart-sweetness and a rich purple hue. Excellent as a glaze for roast meats or a filling for doughnuts.
reference.storage: Fridge.
reference.usageTips: Mix 2 tablespoons of plum jam with a teaspoon of soy sauce and a little ginger to create an instant 'Asian-style' glaze for pork chops or chicken wings.

reference.notes: Poppy seeds are tiny, oil-rich seeds with a subtle nutty flavor. - ** Lightly toast to enhance aroma and crunch. - **Pairings:** Complements lemon, orange, almond, vanilla, honey, and cream cheese. - ** Can be refrigerated or frozen for longer shelf life. - **Substitutions:** Sesame seeds or finely chopped nuts can provide similar texture and crunch in recipes.
reference.purpose: Adds nutty flavor, crunch, and visual appeal to baked goods and desserts.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dark place in an airtight container.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use whole or ground in cakes, muffins, pastries, breads, and desserts.

reference.notes: Pork is a versatile red meat used in a wide variety of dishes. - ** Marinate for flavor when grilling, roasting, stir-frying, or braising. Can be ground for sausages, dumplings, or meatballs. - **Pairings:** Complements garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, citrus, herbs, and spices. - ** Thaw safely before cooking. - **Tips:** Trim excess fat if desired; slow cooking enhances tenderness and flavor. Ensure pork is fully cooked to safe internal temperature.
reference.purpose: Provides rich, savory protein and fat; adds flavor, moisture, and texture to Filipino and international dishes such as stews, adobo, roasts, stir-fries, and sausages.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store fresh pork in the refrigerator and use within 2–3 days; freeze for longer storage.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use cuts according to cooking method—loin, belly, shoulder, or ribs.

reference.notes: Chops are usually cut from the loin. They can be 'Bone-in' (more flavor) or 'Boneless' (easier to eat).
reference.purpose: A classic, lean, and fast-cooking protein. They offer a mild flavor that pairs perfectly with fruit (like apples or plums).
reference.storage: Fridge; 2 days.
reference.usageTips: To prevent pork chops from curling up in the pan, make small vertical cuts (snips) through the fat on the edge of the chop every 2 centimeters. This stops the fat from shrinking and pulling the meat out of shape.

reference.notes: The leg is a large muscle group. It is leaner than the shoulder, so it benefits from being roasted to exactly 'medium' to stay juicy.
reference.purpose: The best cut for achieving the perfect 'Aussie Pork Crackling.' It provides a massive amount of lean, tender meat.
reference.storage: Fridge; 3 days.
reference.usageTips: For the best crackling: The skin MUST be bone-dry. Pour boiling water over the skin, pat it dry with a paper towel, then leave it uncovered in the fridge overnight before roasting. Rub with plenty of salt just before it goes in the oven.

reference.notes: Pork mince is the secret to soft meatballs and dumplings. It has a higher fat content than beef, which prevents 'dry' results.
reference.purpose: Provides a rich, savory fat content and a fine texture. It is often mixed with other meats to add juiciness.
reference.storage: Use within 24 hours. Pork spoils faster than beef.
reference.usageTips: Mix pork and beef mince 50/50 for your Bolognese or Sausage Rolls. The beef provides the structure, and the pork provides the moisture and flavor.

reference.notes: Also known as 'Pork Butt' or 'Boston Butt.' It is full of fat and connective tissue that dissolves into succulent gelatin after hours of cooking.
reference.purpose: The ultimate cut for 'Low and Slow' cooking. It is the only cut for authentic Pulled Pork.
reference.storage: Keeps well in the freezer for up to 6 months.
reference.usageTips: Do not trim the fat cap! Let it sit on top during cooking; the fat will melt down through the meat, acting as a natural basting agent.

reference.notes: Pork stock is the unsung hero of the kitchen. It has a natural sweetness that pairs perfectly with ginger and soy sauce.
reference.purpose: Provides a lighter, sweeter, and cleaner savory base than beef stock. Essential for many Asian noodle soups.
reference.storage: Freeze for up to 3 months.
reference.usageTips: When making pork stock, blanch the bones in boiling water for 5 minutes first, then discard that water and start fresh. This removes the 'scum' and ensures your final stock is perfectly clear.

reference.notes: Harder to find than beef or chicken cubes, but worth searching for if you want a lighter, cleaner savory flavor.
reference.purpose: Provides an instant savory-sweet boost. Excellent for quick Asian soups or enhancing a pork-based gravy.
reference.storage: Keep dry.
reference.usageTips: Crumble a pork stock cube into your water when boiling potatoes for a mash—it adds a background savory depth that salt alone can't achieve.

reference.notes: Usually sliced from the 'Loin' or 'Fillet.' Because these are lean muscles, they can become tough if overcooked.
reference.purpose: A fast-cooking, lean protein base for stir-fries and noodle dishes.
reference.storage: Use within 24 hours.
reference.usageTips: To keep pork strips tender, use the 'Velveting' technique: toss the raw strips in 1 teaspoon of cornflour and a splash of soy sauce 10 minutes before cooking. The cornflour creates a protective barrier that keeps the juices inside.

reference.notes: Potatoes are versatile tubers with starchy or waxy flesh. - **Regular Potatoes:** Varieties include Desiree (red skin, all-rounder), Sebago (high starch, ideal for chips and mash), Dutch Cream (yellow flesh, rich and creamy), Kipfler (waxy, good for salads and roasting), Pontiac (red skin, good boiler), and King Edward (floury, excellent for baking). Waxy types hold shape in salads and stews; floury types break down for mash, gnocchi, and baking. - **Sweet Potatoes / Kumara:** Varieties include Beauregard (orange, moist, very sweet), Jewel (orange, slightly firmer), Garnet (deep orange-red skin, rich flavour), Kumara Orange (classic roasting), Kumara Gold (golden flesh, nutty, drier), Kumara Purple (purple skin and flesh, dense, less sweet), and Kumara White (pale flesh, mild and dry). Moist orange varieties are best for mashing and baking; drier white or purple types are ideal for roasting and frying. - ** Can be incorporated into doughs or gnocchi. - **Pairings:** Complements butter, cream, cheese, garlic, herbs, cinnamon, nutmeg, maple, and honey. - ** Do not store near onions.
reference.purpose: Neutral or sweet starchy base; adds texture, moisture, and natural flavour to mashes, roasts, fries, bakes, gratins, soups, and doughs. Provides versatility in both sweet and savory dishes.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dark, dry place; avoid refrigeration for regular potatoes (affects texture) and keep sweet potatoes in a well-ventilated area.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Boil, roast, bake, mash, fry, or use in soups and gratins.

reference.notes: Usually sold as 'Washed' potatoes in supermarkets. Varieties like Coliban or Nadine are common white potatoes in Australia.
reference.purpose: A versatile, mid-starch potato. It holds its shape better than brushed potatoes, making it ideal for boiling and salads.
reference.storage: Store in a dark, cool place. Never keep potatoes in the fridge, as the cold turns their starch into sugar, making them taste weirdly sweet and turn dark when fried.
reference.usageTips: Because they have a waxy skin, these are the best choice for a 'Creamy Potato Salad.' They won't crumble apart when you toss them with the dressing.

reference.notes: There are over 4,000 varieties of potato! In the kitchen, we group them into 'Starchy' (good for mash/roasting) and 'Waxy' (good for salads/boiling).
reference.purpose: The foundational starch of the Western kitchen. They provide bulk, comfort, and an endless variety of textures.
reference.storage: Cool, dark, and dry. Do not refrigerate, as it ruins the texture and flavor.
reference.usageTips: If you don't know which potato you have, look at the skin. Generally, thick, dusty skins (Brushed) are for mashing; thin, smooth, or red skins are for boiling and salads.

reference.notes: Prawns are high in protein and very low in fat. They change color from gray (raw) to bright pink/orange when they are cooked.
reference.purpose: A fast-cooking, sweet, and delicate seafood protein.
reference.storage: Use within 24 hours of purchase. For the best flavor, buy them with the shells still on and peel them right before cooking.
reference.usageTips: The 2-minute rule: Prawns only take about 2 minutes to cook. The moment they curl into a 'C' shape, they are perfect. If they curl into a tight 'O', they are overcooked and will be rubbery.

reference.notes: Prosciutto is raw ham that has been cured with salt and air-dried for up to 2 years. It is designed to be eaten paper-thin.
reference.purpose: Provides an intense, salty, and silky savory hit. It is the ultimate luxury deli meat for platters and wrapping.
reference.storage: Keep cold. Use within 2-3 days of opening, as it dries out and becomes tough very quickly.
reference.usageTips: Don't cook it too long! If you fry prosciutto, it becomes incredibly salty. It is best used as a finishing touch, or wrapped around asparagus or chicken just before the very end of roasting.

reference.notes: Psyllium is a soluble fiber that absorbs water to form a thick gel. It mimics the 'chew' that gluten usually provides in bread.
reference.purpose: Provides a massive boost of dietary fiber and acts as a structural 'binder' in gluten-free or low-carb baking.
reference.storage: Keep dry. It is highly sensitive to humidity.
reference.usageTips: In gluten-free bread recipes, always let the dough 'hydrate' for 10 minutes after adding the psyllium. This gives the husk time to absorb the water and create the structure needed for the loaf.

reference.notes: Made by layering dough and butter (a process called lamination). When the cold butter hits the hot oven, it creates steam which puffs the layers apart.
reference.purpose: Provides hundreds of light, buttery, and flaky layers. It is the gold standard for pies, tarts, and sausage rolls.
reference.storage: Keep frozen until ready to use. Once thawed, use within 24 hours and do not re-freeze the raw dough.
reference.usageTips: The secret to puff pastry is keeping it **cold**. If it gets too warm, the butter melts into the dough and it won't puff. If it starts to feel sticky, put it back in the fridge for 10 minutes before continuing.

reference.notes: Pumpkins are versatile winter squash with sweet, firm flesh suitable for baking, roasting, and pureeing. - ** Different varieties vary in sweetness, moisture, and texture. - **Varieties:** * **Butternut Pumpkin:** Sweet, creamy, smooth texture; great for soups and baking. * **Crown Pumpkin:** Dense, slightly sweet; holds shape well for roasting. * **Jap Pumpkin:** Sweet, dry, and dense; ideal for baking and mashing. * **Kabocha:** Sweet, nutty flavor; firm, dense flesh. * **Red Kuri:** Mildly sweet, rich orange flesh; good for pies and soups. * **Sugar Pumpkin:** Classic baking pumpkin; moderately sweet and moist. * **White Pumpkin:** Mildly sweet, pale flesh; versatile for baking or roasting. - ** Once cut, wrap and refrigerate; use within a few days.
reference.purpose: Adds natural sweetness, moisture, vibrant colour, and creamy texture to baked goods, pies, muffins, breads, soups, and purees. Contributes flavour, nutrition, and visual appeal.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store whole pumpkins in a cool, dry place.
reference.usageTips: Usage:** Use roasted, mashed, or pureed in pies, muffins, breads, soups, stews, or gnocchi.

reference.notes: Refer to Pumpkin entry in inventory for kernel details.
reference.purpose: Adds crunch, texture, protein, healthy fats, and micronutrients.

reference.notes: Also known as 'Pouring Cream.' It has a lower fat content than thickened cream and is best for pouring over desserts or adding to coffee.
reference.purpose: Provides a clean, dairy richness. It is the 'purest' form of cream with no added thickeners or stabilizers.
reference.storage: Store in the coldest part of the fridge. It is very sensitive to temperature changes.
reference.usageTips: This is the best cream for making homemade butter! Just put it in a jar and shake it (or use a mixer) until the fat solids separate from the buttermilk.

reference.notes: Quinoa is a versatile, gluten-free pseudo-grain known for its high protein and nutritional value. - **Common Varieties and Can be cooked, toasted, or added whole to breads, granola, salads, and gluten-free baking for color and texture. * **White Quinoa:** Milder flavour; cooks faster and softer. Can be used cooked, flaked, or ground into flour for breads, muffins, and other gluten-free baked goods. - **Usage Tips:** Rinse thoroughly before cooking to remove natural saponins that can taste bitter. Toast lightly to enhance nuttiness. Adjust hydration in recipes when using whole or flaked quinoa for optimal texture. - ** Can also be stored in the fridge for longer shelf life.
reference.purpose: Adds protein, texture, structure, and visual interest to breads, baked goods, and gluten-free recipes. Provides a slightly nutty flavour, improves bite, and enhances nutritional profile with fibre, minerals, and essential amino acids.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to prevent moisture and pests.
reference.usageTips:
Usage:**
  * **Black Quinoa:** Darker color; slightly earthier, nuttier flavour.

reference.notes: Radishes are part of the mustard family, which explains that 'spicy' bite they have when raw.
reference.purpose: Adds a sharp, peppery crunch and a beautiful pop of pink color to salads and tacos.
reference.storage: Cut the green leaves off before storing! The leaves suck the moisture out of the radish, making it go 'spongy' in 24 hours.
reference.usageTips: If your radishes taste too 'bitey' or sharp, try roasting them whole with olive oil and salt. The heat destroys the pepperiness and turns them sweet and juicy, almost like a turnip.

reference.notes: Raisins are dried red or purple grapes. Because they are dried for longer than sultanas, they are darker and less juicy.
reference.purpose: Adds a deep, dark sweetness and a chewy texture. They are more intense and 'musky' than sultanas.
reference.storage: Store airtight.
reference.usageTips: Raisins are the best choice for savory dishes like Moroccan Tagines or Indian Pilafs, as their flavor stands up better to strong spices than sweet sultanas.

reference.notes: Delicate, sweet-tart berries that pair beautifully with vanilla, chocolate, and cream desserts. Best used fresh or frozen. Do not wash until ready to use.
reference.purpose: Adds bright, tart flavour and vibrant colour to desserts, breakfast dishes, and sauces.
reference.storage: Store in the refrigerator in a single layer, unwashed, for up to 2-3 days. Freeze in a single layer on a baking sheet, then transfer to a sealed bag.
reference.substitutes: Can substitute with blackberries, sliced strawberries, or frozen raspberries (thawed and drained).
reference.usageTips: Use fresh as a garnish, purée into sauces, fold into cake batters, or simmer into jams. Complements vanilla, chocolate, lemon, and cream.

reference.notes: Raspberry jam is famous for its tiny seeds. If you hate the seeds, look for 'Seedless' or 'Sieved' raspberry conserve.
reference.purpose: Adds a sophisticated, tart fruitiness and a bright ruby color. It is more 'aromatic' than strawberry jam.
reference.storage: Refrigerate after opening.
reference.usageTips: Raspberry jam is the traditional choice for a classic 'Victoria Sponge' cake. Its high acidity cuts through the heavy cream and butter better than any other jam.

reference.notes: Also known as a 'Bell Pepper.' They are packed with more Vitamin C than an orange!
reference.purpose: Adds a vibrant color and a sweet, mild pepper flavor. Red capsicums are fully ripe and much sweeter than green ones.
reference.storage: Store in the crisper drawer. If they start to go soft, they are still perfect for roasting or stews.
reference.usageTips: To remove the skin for a silky sauce, char the capsicum over a gas flame until the skin is black, then seal in a bowl for 10 minutes. The skin will peel right off.

reference.notes: Cayenne is one of the most common chillies globally. It has a thin wall, which makes it perfect for drying and grinding into the famous spice powder.
reference.purpose: Adds a sharp, immediate heat and a bright red color. It is a 'clean' heat that doesn't linger as long as Habanero or Scotch Bonnet.
reference.storage: Store in the fridge.
reference.usageTips: If you want the beautiful red color in your stir-fry but only a mild heat, cut the chilli in half lengthwise and scrape out every single seed. The 'burn' is concentrated in the white ribs and the seeds.

reference.notes: Red chili comes in whole, dried, or ground forms and adds heat, colour, and aroma to a wide range of dishes. - **Forms and Ideal for tempering, pickling, or slow-cooked curries and stews. * **Red Chili Powder / Ground Chili:** Made from dried red chilies; provides even intensity in sauces, curries, rubs, and marinades. Hot paprika can substitute for mild heat and colour. - **Usage Tips:** Remove seeds to reduce heat if desired. Toast whole chilies lightly to enhance aroma before grinding. Start with small amounts and adjust to taste. - **
reference.purpose: Provides heat, aroma, and vibrant red colour to curries, sauces, stir-fries, and spice blends.
reference.storage: Storage:** Store in airtight containers away from sunlight and moisture to preserve colour, flavour, and pungency.
reference.usageTips:
Usage:**
  * **Whole Dried Red Chili:** Use whole, crushed, or toasted; adds heat and aroma gradually.

reference.notes: These are usually made from dried and crushed Cayenne peppers. Because they are dried, the heat is more concentrated than fresh chilli.
reference.purpose: Provides a controllable, easy-to-measure heat. Perfect for adding 'fire' to pasta sauces, pizzas, and marinades.
reference.storage: Pantry. Replace if they turn a dull brown; they should be a bright, fiery red.
reference.usageTips: Always add chilli flakes to your hot oil or butter at the start of cooking (the 'blooming' phase). This infuses the fat with spice, ensuring the heat is distributed evenly through the whole dish.

reference.notes: Be careful: 'Red Chilli Powder' is pure ground chillies. It is much hotter than 'Chilli Powder' (which is usually a blend containing cumin and garlic).
reference.purpose: Adds a vibrant red hue and a deep, building heat. Essential for authentic curries and Mexican spice rubs.
reference.storage: Keep in a dark spot to prevent the color from fading.
